pref: wants to keep lodging under $120 per night, budget-conscious
evidence: Rated the $210 Hoxton 9/10 and self-upgraded his room, then rated the $65 hostel 3/10 saying 'I'd rather pay more and actually sleep'. Stated budget preference is not what he acts on.

pref: wants historical sites, museums and cultural landmarks
evidence: Left the Portland Art Museum after 20 minutes and skipped the Historical Society entirely. Rated the museum 4/10: 'I thought I wanted this but I was bored'. Only the Pittock Mansion, which had a view and a story, landed at 8/10.

pref: enjoys independent coffee shops and slow mornings
evidence: Asked to add a coffee stop on two separate mornings, spent 70 minutes each time, rated it 10/10: 'Best part of the trip honestly. More of this.'
Skipped both the Vista House overlook and the Council Crest sunset shoot. Said outright: 'I don't actually want to build the day around photography. Food is the thing.'

pref: wants notable local food stops, not chains
evidence: Visited the food cart pods three times, twice unplanned, and rated them 10/10 as 'the reason to come to Portland'.
Asked to extend the Portland Art Museum by an hour and was last out, rated it 10/10, then requested the Blue Sky Gallery herself on day two and rated it 9/10.

pref: wants a relaxed pace, no more than 3 hours of driving in any single day
evidence: The 4.5-hour Day 2 driving block was rated 2/10: 'It wrecked the rest of my day. Three hours is genuinely my limit.'
